newsitem.title: GREECE: Forex inflows firm drachma, short forwards drop.
newsitem.headline: Forex inflows firm drachma, short forwards drop.

text.p: Forex inflows strengthened the drachma vis-a-vis the ECU and pushed short-term forex forwards down 15 basis points.
Depos were easier with the central bank pumping overnight cash at 13.40 percent to close the liquidity gap.

"The highlight of the day was the heavy forex inflows that sent short forex forwards 15 basis points lower. Depos were also easier," said a forex trader at a foreign bank. "The Bank of Greece injected overnight cash at 13.40 percent again."
Traders said they expected the market to turn long if forex inflows continued at the same pace. They said about 300 million ecus, 100 million marks and $65 million were sold at the fixing.
"I think the market will turn long on September 9 after these inflows," said a money trader at a state bank.
Some traders said the inflows showed confidence in the hard drachma policy of the central bank, but others warned this was hot money that could leave the system anytime.
"The nature of these short-term inflows is just speculative," said a dealer at a foreign bank. "Inflows linked to FRN purchases are of a more permanent nature."
The mark was quoted at 157.21/26 drachmas from Monday's 157.250 fix, the dollar at 240.72/82 drachmas from 240.750 and the Ecu at 300.79/89 from 300.800 drachmas.
"The drachma has firmed versus the ecu and other currencies on the back of heavy sale of ecus and other currencies for drachmas," said a dealer at a foreing bank.
